label.en: Definition 8.1 — Exponent Rules, Radicals, and Logarithmic Foundations
label.ar: تعريف 8.1 — Exponent Rules, Radicals, and Logarithmic Foundations

body.en:
Core algebraic rules governing exponents, radicals, and logarithms:
  • Fundamental Laws of Exponents: For base \(a > 0\) and real exponents \(m, n\):
    1. Product Rule: \(a^m \cdot a^n = a^{m+n}\)
    2. Quotient Rule: \(\frac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}\)
    3. Power of a Power: \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\)
    4. Power of a Product: \((ab)^n = a^n b^n\)
    5. Negative Exponent: \(a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}\) (reciprocal, not negative value)
    6. Zero Exponent: \(a^0 = 1\) (for \(a \neq 0\))
  • Rational Exponents and Radical Equivalence:
    \[ a^{m/n} = \sqrt[n]{a^m} = (\sqrt[n]{a})^m \]
    The denominator \(n\) is the radical index (root), and the numerator \(m\) is the exponent power.
  • Definition of Logarithm: For base \(b > 0, b \neq 1\) and argument \(x > 0\):
    \[ \log_b(x) = y \iff b^y = x \]
    1. Common Logarithm: \(\log(x) = \log_{10}(x)\).
    2. Natural Logarithm: \(\ln(x) = \log_e(x)\), where Euler's number \(e \approx 2.71828\).
  • Exponential Growth and Decay Models:
    1. Discrete periodic model: \(A(t) = A_0 (1 \pm r)^t\), where \(A_0\) is the initial amount, \(r\) is the growth/decay rate per period, and \(t\) is the number of periods.
    2. Doubling time / Half-life model: \(A(t) = A_0 \cdot 2^{t/T_d}\) or \(A(t) = A_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/T_{1/2}}\).

body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.

For logarithmic and radical المعادلات, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the الحل set, requiring a final المجال check against the original المعادلة.

label.en: Theorem 8.1 — Logarithm Operational Laws, Change of Base, and Equation Solving
label.ar: مبرهنة 8.1 — Logarithm Operational Laws, Change of Base, and المعادلة Solving

body.en:
Operational laws and solution strategies for transcendental equations:
  • Logarithmic Operational Laws (for \(x, y > 0\)):
    1. Product Law: \(\log_b(xy) = \log_b(x) + \log_b(y)\)
    2. Quotient Law: \(\log_b\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = \log_b(x) - \log_b(y)\)
    3. Power Law: \(\log_b(x^k) = k \cdot \log_b(x)\)
    4. Inverse Identities: \(b^{\log_b(x)} = x\) and \(\log_b(b^x) = x\)
    5. Change of Base Formula: \(\log_b(x) = \frac{\log_c(x)}{\log_c(b)} = \frac{\ln(x)}{\ln(b)}\)
  • Solving Exponential Equations:
    1. Common Base Method: Express both sides as powers of the same base \(b\):
    \[ b^{f(x)} = b^{g(x)} \iff f(x) = g(x) \]
    2. Logarithm Method: Take the natural log of both sides when common bases are unavailable:
    \[ a^x = c \implies \ln(a^x) = \ln(c) \implies x \ln(a) = \ln(c) \implies x = \frac{\ln(c)}{\ln(a)} \]
  • Extraneous Solutions in Logarithmic Equations: When solving equations by combining logarithmic terms, always substitute candidate roots into the original expressions: the argument of every logarithm must be strictly positive (\(x > 0\)). Any root yielding a non-positive argument is extraneous.
body.ar:
Operational laws and الحل strategies for transcendental المعادلات:
  • Logarithmic Operational Laws (for \(x, y > 0\)):
    1. Product Law: \(\log_b(xy) = \log_b(x) + \log_b(y)\)
    2. Quotient Law: \(\log_b\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = \log_b(x) - \log_b(y)\)
    3. Power Law: \(\log_b(x^k) = k \cdot \log_b(x)\)
    4. Inverse المتطابقات: \(b^{\log_b(x)} = x\) and \(\log_b(b^x) = x\)
    5. Change of Base الصيغة: \(\log_b(x) = \frac{\log_c(x)}{\log_c(b)} = \frac{\ln(x)}{\ln(b)}\)
  • Solving Exponential المعادلات:
    1. Common Base Method: Express both sides as powers of the same base \(b\):
    \[ b^{f(x)} = b^{g(x)} \iff f(x) = g(x) \]
    2. Logarithm Method: Take the natural log of both sides عندما common bases are unavailable:
    \[ a^x = c \implies \ln(a^x) = \ln(c) \implies x \ln(a) = \ln(c) \implies x = \frac{\ln(c)}{\ln(a)} \]
  • Extraneous الحلول in Logarithmic المعادلات: عندما solving المعادلات by combining logarithmic terms, always عوّض candidate roots into the original expressions: the argument of every logarithm must be strictly positive (\(x > 0\)). Any root yielding a non-positive argument is extraneous.

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Exponentials & Radicals
label.ar: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Exponentials & Radicals (الدوال الأسية واللوغاريتمية)

body.en:
• Negative Exponents vs. Negative Values: A negative exponent denotes reciprocal, not a negative quantity: \(x^{-n} = \frac{1}{x^n}\). For instance, \(3^{-2} = \frac{1}{9}\), NOT \(-9\) or \(-6\).
  • Fractional Exponent Definition: \(x^{m/n} = \sqrt[n]{x^m} = (\sqrt[n]{x})^m\). The denominator is the index of the radical root, and the numerator is the power: \(8^{2/3} = (\sqrt[3]{8})^2 = 2^2 = 4\).
  • Adding Exponents vs. Multiplying Powers: Remember that \(x^a \cdot x^b = x^{a+b}\), but \((x^a)^b = x^{ab}\). Do not confuse \(2^3 \cdot 2^4 = 2^7\) with \((2^3)^4 = 2^{12}\).
  • Non-Distributivity of Logarithms: Remember that \(\log(x + y) \neq \log x + \log y\)! The product rule states that \(\log(xy) = \log x + \log y\). Similarly, \(\frac{\log x}{\log y} \neq \log(x - y)\).
  • Extraneous Solutions in Radical Equations: Squaring both sides of an equation like \(\sqrt{2x + 3} = x\) can introduce extraneous roots. You MUST substitute candidate roots back into the original unsquared equation to verify validity.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Exponentials & Logarithms)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Exponentials & Logarithms)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

label.en: Worked Example 8.A — Exponential Equation with Common Base Transformation
label.ar: مثال محلول 8.A — Exponential المعادلة with Common Base Transformation

body.en:
Solve the exponential equation \(\left(\dfrac{1}{27}\right)^{x - 2} = 9^{2x + 1}\) for \(x\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Express both sides with prime base 3:
    Recall that \(\frac{1}{27} = 27^{-1} = (3^3)^{-1} = 3^{-3}\) and \(9 = 3^2\).
    Substitute these base representations:
    \[ (3^{-3})^{x - 2} = (3^2)^{2x + 1} \]
  2. Apply the power of a power rule:
    \[ 3^{-3(x - 2)} = 3^{2(2x + 1)} \implies 3^{-3x + 6} = 3^{4x + 2} \]
  3. Equate the exponents:
    Since the bases are identical and non-zero: \[ -3x + 6 = 4x + 2 \implies 6 - 2 = 4x + 3x \implies 4 = 7x \implies \mathbf{x = \frac{4}{7}} \]
The solution is \(\mathbf{x = \frac{4}{7}}\).
body.ar:
Solve the exponential المعادلة \(\left(\dfrac{1}{27}\right)^{x - 2} = 9^{2x + 1}\) for \(x\).

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Express both sides with prime base 3:
    Recall that \(\frac{1}{27} = 27^{-1} = (3^3)^{-1} = 3^{-3}\) and \(9 = 3^2\).
    Substitute these base representations:
    \[ (3^{-3})^{x - 2} = (3^2)^{2x + 1} \]
  2. Apply the power of a power rule:
    \[ 3^{-3(x - 2)} = 3^{2(2x + 1)} \implies 3^{-3x + 6} = 3^{4x + 2} \]
  3. Equate the exponents:
    Since the bases are identical and non-zero: \[ -3x + 6 = 4x + 2 \implies 6 - 2 = 4x + 3x \implies 4 = 7x \implies \mathbf{x = \frac{4}{7}} \]
The الحل is \(\mathbf{x = \frac{4}{7}}\).

label.en: Worked Example 8.B — Half-Life & Exponential Decay Modeling
label.ar: مثال محلول 8.B — Half-Life & Exponential Decay Modeling

body.en:
A radioactive medical isotope has a half-life of 8 days. A laboratory receives an initial shipment containing 640 mg of the isotope.
(a) Write a formula for the remaining mass \(A(t)\) after \(t\) days.
(b) How much of the isotope remains after 24 days?
(c) After how many days will only 10 mg remain?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Formulate the decay model:
    \[ A(t) = A_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/8} = \mathbf{640 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/8}} \]
  2. (b) Mass after 24 days:
    Substitute \(t = 24\):
    \[ A(24) = 640 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{24/8} = 640 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = 640 \times \frac{1}{8} = \mathbf{80\text{ mg}} \]
  3. (c) Time for 10 mg to remain:
    Set \(A(t) = 10\):
    \[ 10 = 640 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/8} \implies \frac{10}{640} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/8} \implies \frac{1}{64} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/8} \]
    Express \(\frac{1}{64}\) as a power of \(\frac{1}{2}\):
    \[ \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^6 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/8} \implies 6 = \frac{t}{8} \implies t = 6 \times 8 = \mathbf{48\text{ days}} \]
Only 10 mg will remain after 48 days.

label.en: Worked Example 8.C — Logarithmic Equation & Extraneous Root Elimination
label.ar: مثال محلول 8.C — Logarithmic المعادلة & Extraneous Root Elimination

body.en:
Solve the logarithmic equation \(\log_2(x + 6) + \log_2(x - 1) = 3\) for all real values of \(x\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Identify the domain of validity:
    Both arguments must be strictly positive:
    \[ x + 6 > 0 \implies x > -6, \qquad x - 1 > 0 \implies x > 1 \implies \text{Domain: } x > 1 \]
  2. Combine terms using the Product Law:
    \[ \log_2[(x + 6)(x - 1)] = 3 \]
  3. Convert to equivalent exponential form:
    \[ (x + 6)(x - 1) = 2^3 = 8 \]
  4. Expand and solve the quadratic:
    \[ x^2 + 5x - 6 = 8 \implies x^2 + 5x - 14 = 0 \implies (x + 7)(x - 2) = 0 \]
    Tentative roots: \(x = 2\) or \(x = -7\).
  5. Check candidate roots in original equation:
    For \(x = 2\): \(\log_2(8) + \log_2(1) = 3 + 0 = 3\) (Valid ✓).
    For \(x = -7\): \(x - 1 = -8 \le 0\) (Undefined logarithm, extraneous root ✗).
The only valid real solution is \(\mathbf{x = 2}\).

body.en:
Problem (Medium): The graph of the exponential function \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \) passes through the points \( (1, 6) \) and \( (2, 18) \). Determine the value of \( a \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Let the function be \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \). We are given two points that lie on the graph: 1. \( (1, 6) \): Substituting these values into the function equation, we get \( 6 = a \cdot b^1 \), which simplifies to \( 6 = ab \). 2. \( (2, 18) \): Substituting these values into the function equation, we get \( 18 = a \cdot b^2 \). We now have a system of two equations with two unknowns, \( a \) and \( b \): (1) \( ab = 6 \) (2) \( ab^2 = 18 \) To solve for \( a \) and \( b \), we can divide equation (2) by equation (1): \[ \frac{ab^2}{ab} = \frac{18}{6} \] \[ b = 3 \] Now that we have the value of \( b \), we can substitute it back into equation (1) to find \( a \): \[ a \cdot (3) = 6 \] \[ a = \frac{6}{3} \] \[ a = 2 \] Therefore, the value of \( a \) is 2.
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): The التمثيل البياني of the exponential الدالة \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \) passes through the points \( (1, 6) \) and \( (2, 18) \). حدّد value of \( a \).

Step-by-Step الحل: Let the الدالة be \( f(x) = a \cdot b^x \). We are المعطيات two points that lie on the التمثيل البياني: 1. \( (1, 6) \): Substituting these values into the الدالة المعادلة, we get \( 6 = a \cdot b^1 \), which simplifies to \( 6 = ab \). 2. \( (2, 18) \): Substituting these values into the الدالة المعادلة, we get \( 18 = a \cdot b^2 \). We now have a system of two المعادلات with two unknowns, \( a \) and \( b \): (1) \( ab = 6 \) (2) \( ab^2 = 18 \) To أوجد قيمة \( a \) and \( b \), we can divide المعادلة (2) by المعادلة (1): \[ \frac{ab^2}{ab} = \frac{18}{6} \] \[ b = 3 \] Now that we have the value of \( b \), we can عوّض it back into المعادلة (1) to find \( a \): \[ a \cdot (3) = 6 \] \[ a = \frac{6}{3} \] \[ a = 2 \] وبالتالي, the value of \( a \) is 2.

question.en: Simplify the expression \(\left(\dfrac{16 x^8 y^{-4}}{81 z^{12}}\right)^{-3/4}\) and write your answer using only positive exponents.
question.ar: بسّط العبارة the expression \(\left(\dfrac{16 x^8 y^{-4}}{81 z^{12}}\right)^{-3/4}\) and write your answer using only positive exponents.

solution.en:
Step 1: Invert the fraction to remove the negative exponent: \[ \left(\frac{16 x^8 y^{-4}}{81 z^{12}}\right)^{-3/4} = \left(\frac{81 z^{12}}{16 x^8 y^{-4}}\right)^{3/4} = \left(\frac{81 y^4 z^{12}}{16 x^8}\right)^{3/4}. \]

Step 2: Take the 4th root of each factor: \[ \left(\frac{81 y^4 z^{12}}{16 x^8}\right)^{1/4} = \frac{81^{1/4} (y^4)^{1/4} (z^{12})^{1/4}}{16^{1/4} (x^8)^{1/4}} = \frac{3 y z^3}{2 x^2}. \]

Step 3: Cube the result: \[ \left(\frac{3 y z^3}{2 x^2}\right)^3 = \frac{3^3 y^3 (z^3)^3}{2^3 (x^2)^3} = \mathbf{\frac{27 y^3 z^9}{8 x^6}}. \]
solution.ar:

Step 2: Take the 4th root of each حلّل: \[ \left(\frac{81 y^4 z^{12}}{16 x^8}\right)^{1/4} = \frac{81^{1/4} (y^4)^{1/4} (z^{12})^{1/4}}{16^{1/4} (x^8)^{1/4}} = \frac{3 y z^3}{2 x^2}. \]

question.en: A population of bacteria in a petri dish starts with 250 organisms and quadruples every 5 hours. How many hours will it take for the population to reach 16,000?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Exponentials & Logarithms): A population of bacteria in a petri dish starts with 250 organisms and quadruples every 5 hours. How many hours will it take for the population to reach 16,000?

solution.en:
Step 1: Set up the exponential growth equation: \[ P(t) = 250 \times 4^{t/5} = 16000. \]

Step 2: Divide both sides by 250: \[ 4^{t/5} = \frac{16000}{250} = \frac{1600}{25} = 64. \]

Step 3: Express 64 as a power of 4: \[ 64 = 4^3 \implies 4^{t/5} = 4^3 \implies \frac{t}{5} = 3 \implies t = 15\text{ hours}. \]

It will take exactly 15 hours.

question.en: Solve the equation \(5 e^{0.04 t} = 45\) for \(t\) in terms of natural logarithms, and find its value rounded to two decimal places.
question.ar: حل المعادلة \(5 e^{0.04 t} = 45\) for \(t\) in terms of natural logarithms, and أوجد its value rounded to two منازل عشرية.

solution.en:
Step 1: Isolate the exponential expression: \[ e^{0.04 t} = \frac{45}{5} = 9. \]

Step 2: Take the natural logarithm of both sides: \[ \ln(e^{0.04 t}) = \ln(9) \implies 0.04 t = \ln(9). \]

Step 3: Solve for \(t\): \[ t = \frac{\ln(9)}{0.04} = 25 \ln(9) = 25 \ln(3^2) = 50 \ln(3) \approx 50(1.0986) = \mathbf{54.93}. \]

The exact solution is \(\mathbf{50\ln(3)}\) (approximately 54.93).

question.en: Solve the logarithmic equation \(\log_3(x^2 - 7) = 2\) for all real solutions, and verify that all roots lie within the valid domain.
question.ar: حل the logarithmic equation \(\log_3(x^2 - 7) = 2\) for all real solutions, and verإذا كانy that all roots lie within the valid domain.

solution.en:
Step 1: Convert to exponential form: \[ x^2 - 7 = 3^2 = 9. \]

Step 2: Solve the quadratic equation: \[ x^2 = 9 + 7 = 16 \implies x = \pm 4. \]

Step 3: Verify the domain \(x^2 - 7 > 0\): For both \(x = 4\) and \(x = -4\): \[ x^2 - 7 = 16 - 7 = 9 > 0. \] Both roots are valid.

The solutions are \(\mathbf{x = 4}\) and \(\mathbf{x = -4}\).

question.en: If \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), what is the value of \( x \)?

hints.en: To solve the equation \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), express both sides in terms of a common base: 1. Recognize that both \( 9 \) and \( 27 \) are powers of \( 3 \):.
hints.ar: To حل المعادلة \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), express both sides in terms of a common base: 1. Recognize that both \( 9 \) and \( 27 \) are powers of \( 3 \):.

hints.en: Rewrite and simplify to obtain: \(9 = 3^2 \quad \text{and} \quad 27 = 3^3\) Substitute these into the original equation: \((3^2)^{x+1} = (3^3)^{x-1}\).
hints.ar: أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \(9 = 3^2 \quad \text{and} \quad 27 = 3^3\) عوّض these into the original equation: \((3^2)^{x+1} = (3^3)^{x-1}\).

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(2 + 3 = 3x - 2x\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(2 + 3 = 3x - 2x\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
To solve the equation \( 9^{x+1} = 27^{x-1} \), express both sides in terms of a common base:

1. Recognize that both \( 9 \) and \( 27 \) are powers of \( 3 \):
   \[ 9 = 3^2 \quad \text{and} \quad 27 = 3^3 \]

2. Substitute these into the original equation:
   \[ (3^2)^{x+1} = (3^3)^{x-1} \]

3. Use the power of a power rule, \( (a^m)^n = a^{mn} \), distributing across both terms in each exponent:
   \[ 3^{2(x+1)} = 3^{3(x-1)} \]
   \[ 3^{2x+2} = 3^{3x-3} \]

4. Since the bases are equal and positive (and not equal to 1), equate the exponents:
   \[ 2x + 2 = 3x - 3 \]
   \[ 2 + 3 = 3x - 2x \]
   \[ x = 5 \]

Common misconceptions:
- Forgetting to distribute the factor to the constant term (e.g., writing \( 2x + 1 = 3x - 1 \)) yields \( x = 2 \).
- Treating the bases as linear multipliers (e.g., \( 9(x+1) = 27(x-1) \)) also incorrectly leads to \( x = 2 \).

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
الأسية\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)تقارب أفقي \(y = k\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, a+k)\)
اللوغاريتمية\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h+1, k)\)
